newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank eases foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank eases foreign investment.

text.p: The Cypriot Central Bank on Monday said it was easing restrictions on foreign investment, part of a liberalisation of investment laws to support the island's application to join the European Union.
Bank officials on Sunday said that foreign investment of up to 100 percent would be allowed in secondary industries, retail and wholesale trading and the service sector.

The new policy relaxes a 1986 law that in most cases put a 49 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in these areas and barred foreigners from other sectors. In retail and wholesale trading investors would need to put in at least 300,000 Cyprus pounds ($600,000) to qualify for owning more than 49 percent and at least 50,000 pounds in the service sector.
But in the leisure industry foreigners will be allowed to control only a maximum 49 percent, with minimum investments of at least 60,000 pounds.
Foreigners will have to apply for permission to invest in finance and insurance companies, banks and publications. Previously no foreign investment was allowed in these sectors.
But foreigners are still barred from land development, operating airlines and taking a stake in utility companies.
"In the past applications to invest in traditional industries were rejected, now we are encouraging greater foreign investment," Central Bank official Iacovos Pashos said on Monday.
Limits have also been eased on the amount of money Cypriots can invest abroad. ($1=0.50 Cyprus pounds)
